samples.summary: New merge-budget clamp validates key and cell-count but not span *shape*, so a hostile CRDT merge map still reaches the unbounded cover-map walk it was added to prevent
samples.evidence:
The change adds a defensive clamp in `rebuildMergeCoverMap` whose stated threat model is explicit: "the Yorkie auth webhook authorizes a write by (document, verb) and never inspects an op's content, so anyone holding `rw` on the document can put an arbitrary merge map into it directly" (sheet.ts:866-872). The clamp only spends `mergeBudgetAdmits(budget, [span])` and round-trips the key; it never checks that `span.rs`/`span.cs` are positive integers, and `YorkieStore.getMerges` (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:1072-1074) hands the raw CRDT values through with `{...span}`.

Three concrete bypasses for an attacker with `rw` on a shared document who writes `sheets[tab].merges` directly through the CRDT (no REST validator in the path, so `parseMerges`' integer checks do not apply):

1. Fractional/huge span. `{"A1":{"rs":1e9,"cs":1e-9}}` → `cells = rs*cs ≈ 1`, so `mergeBudgetAdmits` (merging.ts:112-113) admits it, then the walk at sheet.ts:905 `for (let r = anchor.r; r < anchor.r + span.rs; r++)` runs ~1e9 iterations, inserting into `mergeCoverMap` each time → tab hangs/OOMs on every open, for every collaborator, permanently — exactly the failure the budget exists to prevent.
2. NaN poisoning. `{"A1":{}}` (missing `rs`) → `cells = NaN`; `NaN > MaxMergedCells` is false so the span is admitted, and `budget.coveredCells` becomes `NaN` (sheet.ts:903). Every later `mergeBudgetError` comparison against `NaN` is false (merging.ts:90), so `MaxMergeCoveredCells` is silently disabled for the rest of the load and for the cached `this.mergeBudget` used by `canMergeSelection` and `applyPasteMerges` — 10,000 entries × 100,000 cells = 1e9 cover entries then passes.
3. Non-object span. `{"A1":null}` → `span.rs` throws `TypeError` at merging.ts:112, outside the `try` that only wraps `parseRef` (sheet.ts:889-893) → `loadMerges` rejects and the tab fails to open for every collaborator.

The same unvalidated spans flow into `YorkieStore.setMerge`'s `mergeBudgetOf(others)` (yorkie-store.ts:1019), so the store-side floor is poisoned the same way.

samples.summary: `snapFreezePastMerges` calls `parseRef` on stored merge keys with no try/catch, giving `PUT .../freeze` a new permanent 500 on any document whose merge map holds a non-reference key
samples.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges` does `ranges.push(toMergeRange(parseRef(anchorSref), span))` unguarded, and `parseRef` throws `Error('Invalid Reference')` for any key with no digit (coordinates.ts:350-352). The change wires this helper into `ApiV1WorksheetController.setFreeze` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet.controller.ts:121-125), which reads `ws.merges` straight off the CRDT with `safeWorksheetRecordEntries` and performs no key validation — `PUT freeze` previously never touched `merges` at all, so this is a newly reachable crash path. An attacker holding `rw` on the document (the same threat model the diff states for `rebuildMergeCoverMap`, sheet.ts:866-872) writes one entry such as `merges = { "__proto__": {rs:1,cs:1} }` or `{"junk":{rs:2,cs:2}}` directly through Yorkie; every subsequent `PUT /api/v1/.../tabs/:tabId/freeze` on that tab throws inside `doc.update` and answers 500, permanently, for every API client. The engine's own load path was hardened against exactly this key class in this same diff (sheet.ts:889-899), but the shared helper the backend calls was not — so the backend copy is the unguarded entry point. `PUT merges` is not affected (its keys round-trip through `toSref`), and `POST move` / `POST insert` already parsed stored keys before this change.

samples.summary: The new `MaxSnappedFreeze` paintability ceiling is enforced only on the REST writer; the editor/CRDT writer can still persist an arbitrarily deep freeze
samples.evidence: `parseFreeze` now clamps `rows`/`cols` to `MaxSnappedFreeze` (1000) and justifies it as the depth past which the tab "never paints — which also means the user cannot reach the freeze menu to undo it" (worksheet-settings.ts:54-59). That bound is applied to no other writer of the same field: `Sheet.setFreezePane` deliberately passes a caller-requested line through untouched (`snapFreezePastMerges` bounds only *growth*, merging.ts:56-58; sheet.ts:543-548) and `YorkieStore.setFreezePane` writes `root.sheets[tabId].frozenRows = frozenRows` with no validation (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:1204-1216). So a browser client (or anyone with `rw` writing the CRDT field directly) can store `frozenRows = 1000000`, producing the stored, collaborator-wide unpaintable-tab state the validator says it exists to prevent, recoverable only by another API call. A gate on one of several writers reads as covered while the other door stays open. Backend writers of the field are `worksheet-shape-migration.ts:449` and `template/seed/seed-templates.ts:140`, both carrying derived/trusted values, so the REST surface itself is consistent.
searchedFor: grep setFreezePane( across packages/**/*.ts (engine, stores, view, frontend)
grep frozen|ySplit|xSplit|pane in packages/sheets/src/import/xlsx-importer.ts (no freeze writer there)
glob packages/backend/src/api/v1/*.ts for any other sheet-content write endpoint

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. rebuildMergeCoverMap (sheet.ts:880-917) validates only the budget (line 887) and key round-trip (line 900), never the shape of span.rs/span.cs, despite its own comment (sheet.ts:866-872) declaring the threat model to be an arbitrary merge map written straight into the CRDT by anyone with `rw`. mergeBudgetAdmits (merging.ts:104-118) computes cells = span.rs * span.cs and rejects only `cells > MaxMergedCells`, so (a) {rs:1e9, cs:1e-9} or {rs:1e9, cs:0} yields cells <= 1 and is admitted, then the walk at sheet.ts:905 runs ~1e9 iterations; (b) a missing rs yields NaN, which passes every `>` comparison in mergeBudgetError (merging.ts:87-93), poisons budget.coveredCells at sheet.ts:903 and the cached this.mergeBudget at sheet.ts:916 (consumed by canMergeSelection at sheet.ts:4931), disabling MaxMergeCoveredCells; (c) a null span throws TypeError at merging.ts:112, outside the try at sheet.ts:889-893 that wraps only parseRef, so loadMerges (sheet.ts:588-591) rejects. No upstream guard blocks this: YorkieStore.getMerges (yorkie-store.ts:1068-1076) copies raw CRDT values with {...span}, and safeWorksheetRecordEntries (worksheet-record.ts:47-61) is only an Object.entries duplicate-key workaround with no value validation. The integer checks (assertInt on s.rs/s.cs, worksheet-settings.ts:165-173) exist only in parseMerges on the REST path, which a direct CRDT write bypasses; setMerge's floor (yorkie-store.ts:1019 via projectedMerges at 975-980) reads the same unvalidated spans. This is unsafe handling of attacker-controlled input at a named trust boundary, and an added-but-bypassable gate that reads as covered — in lane and blocking.

finding.summary: `snapFreezePastMerges` calls `parseRef` on stored merge keys with no try/catch, giving `PUT .../freeze` a new permanent 500 on any document whose merge map holds a non-reference key
finding.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges` does `ranges.push(toMergeRange(parseRef(anchorSref), span))` unguarded, and `parseRef` throws `Error('Invalid Reference')` for any key with no digit (coordinates.ts:350-352). The change wires this helper into `ApiV1WorksheetController.setFreeze` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet.controller.ts:121-125), which reads `ws.merges` straight off the CRDT with `safeWorksheetRecordEntries` and performs no key validation — `PUT freeze` previously never touched `merges` at all, so this is a newly reachable crash path. verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as claimed: merging.ts:347 calls `parseRef(anchorSref)` unguarded on caller-supplied merge keys, and coordinates.ts:350-352 throws `Invalid Reference` for any key without a digit past index 0. worksheet.controller.ts:121-125 (`PUT freeze`) passes raw CRDT keys via `safeWorksheetRecordEntries`, which (worksheet-record.ts:47-61) only recovers from duplicate-ownKeys TypeErrors and does no key validation, so the throw escapes `doc.update` as a 500. No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable — the analogous hardening exists only in the engine's own reader (sheet.ts:888-900), which sanitizes `this.merges` before its `snapFreezePastMerges` call (sheet.ts:557-562), leaving the shared helper's backend entry points (also worksheet-structure.ts:278-282) unprotected. The repo itself documents the threat model that any `rw` holder can write an arbitrary merge map straight through Yorkie because the auth webhook never inspects op content (sheet.ts:866-872), so the malformed-key write is reachable by an authenticated collaborator and the resulting failure is persistent for every API client of that tab. Missing validation of untrusted stored input causing a durable endpoint failure is in the security lane (unsafe input handling / availability), not merely a style or design concern, so I cannot refute it on not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope grounds.

finding.summary: `PUT .../freeze` still accepts up to 1,000,000 frozen rows, which this change's own reasoning calls an unpaintable tab — a stored client-side DoS the new snap cap explicitly delegates to this validator and this validator does not enforce
finding.evidence: Chain: (1) `parseFreeze` bounds `rows` only at the grid (`max: MaxRows` = 1_000_000, worksheet-settings.ts:61) and `cols` at 18_278. (2) `ApiV1WorksheetController.setFreeze` (worksheet.controller.ts:121-128) passes the requested value through `snapFreezePastMerges`, which by design leaves a caller-requested line untouched — merging.ts:355-362 only bounds *growth*, and its own docstring says "bounding the request is the validator's job (`parseFreeze` in the backend)". (3) The value is persisted verbatim and loaded with no clamp: `Sheet.loadFreezePane` (sheet.ts:567-571) and `YorkieStore.getFreezePane` (yorkie-store.ts:1221-1227). (4) `GridCanvas.render` draws quadrant B/A with `renderQuadrantCells(ctx, 1, fr + 1, ...)` (gridcanvas.ts:329-332, 400-405) and that helper loops `for (let row = rowStart; row <= rowEnd; row++)` over every column (gridcanvas.ts:869, 1754) with no viewport clipping of the loop. Attack: any principal with write scope on the workspace (including a leaked/over-scoped API key) issues one `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:w/documents/:d/tabs/:t/freeze {"rows":1000000}`; every collaborator who opens that tab afterwards builds ~1e6 x visible-columns srefs per frame and the grid never paints — and per `MaxSnappedFreeze`'s own docstring (merging.ts:45-59) the user "cannot reach the freeze menu to undo it". Recovery requires another API call. The 1,000-row ceiling this PR introduces for the *snap* concedes that 100,000 is already fatal, so the direct request path is 1,000x more permissive than the derived path in the same change.

verdict.reason: The finding's core factual claim is false. It states `parseFreeze` bounds `rows` at `MaxRows` = 1_000_000 and `cols` at 18_278, so a 1,000,000-row freeze is accepted and stored. The actual code at packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:72-73 bounds BOTH axes at `MaxSnappedFreeze`: `assertInt(b.rows ?? 0, 'rows', { min: 0, max: MaxSnappedFreeze })` and the same for `cols`. `MaxRows`/`MaxColumns` never appear in `parseFreeze` — they are used only by `parseHidden` (:100-101) and `parseMerges` (:161-172). The cited "worksheet-settings.ts:61" is a line inside the JSDoc block, not a bound. `MaxSnappedFreeze` is 1000 (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts:60), i.e. exactly the ceiling the finding says the snap path uses, so the alleged 1,000x asymmetry between the direct and derived paths does not exist. The controller enforces it on the real request path: worksheet.controller.ts:106 calls `parseFreeze(body)` before `withDocument`/`doc.update`, so `{"rows":1000000}` throws BadRequestException and never reaches `snapFreezePastMerges` (:121-125) or the writes at :126-128. Persistence is bounded on both branches — the snap either passes through an already-validated value (<=1000) or releases the axis to 0 when growth exceeds the ceiling (merging.ts:361). The delegation the finding correctly identifies (merging.ts:56-58 "bounding the request is the validator's job (`parseFreeze` in the backend)") is honored, not dropped; parseFreeze's own docstring (worksheet-settings.ts:64-67) names the 1,000,000-row grid bound as the alternative it deliberately rejects. The reviewer appears to have read that docstring's description of the rejected alternative, or a pre-change state, as the implementation.
